newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans surge, July hits $9.00 on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans surge, July hits $9.00 on Brazil.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures surged in opening trade and the July contract touched the $9.00 per bushel mark, a contract high, for the first time since the 1988 drought on news the U.S. agricultural attache in Brazil lowered crop output projections, traders said.
The U.S. attache put Brazil's soybean output at 26.5 million tonnes, below USDA's April projection for 27 million tonnes. Attache reports often affect USDA monthly supply and demand figures.

The attache report, coupled with strong U.S. and world soybean demand, led traders to speculate USDA would be forced to trim soybean ending stocks estimates in Monday's monthly Supply and Demand Report.
Talk Thursday's USDA export sales figure for soybeans would be above 400,000 tonnes also lent support.

Contract highs were notched in the May and July contracts in early trade. As of 0941 CDT the new high for the July was $9.02 per bushel, topping the previous high of $8.99 set on Monday. The May contract touched $9.03-1/2, the highest for a nearby contract since the 1988 drought.
At 0942 CDT, soybeans were up seven to 4-1/2 cents per bushel with July up five cents at $8.97.
